The default engine fits each model with `glm()`, so the outcome and the
mediator can each take a family. Part of the [Models](models.html) collection.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Structure** | X to M to Y, one model per variable |
| **Class returned** | `MediationData` |
| **Set with** | `family_y = ` and `family_m = ` in `fit_mediation()`, or fit the `glm()` yourself and extract |
| **Scale** | `b` and `c'` are on the outcome's link scale; `a` is on the mediator's |

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
d <- mediation_demo
d$outcome_bin <- as.integer(d$outcome > median(d$outcome))
d$mediator_bin <- as.integer(d$mediator1 > median(d$mediator1))
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Read this first
With a non-identity link, `b` and `c'` are on the link scale, so the product
`a * b` is **not** a natural indirect effect on the outcome scale. medfit
reports the product; the interpretation is yours to defend. See
[Methods and Formulas](methods.html).
:::

## Binary outcome

```{r}
#| label: binary-outcome
fit_y <- fit_mediation(
  outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = d, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
  family_y = binomial()
)
paths(fit_y)
```

Here `b` and `c'` are log odds ratios and `a` is a change in the mediator.

## Binary mediator

```{r}
#| label: binary-mediator
fit_m <- fit_mediation(
  outcome ~ treatment + mediator_bin + covariate1 + covariate2,
  mediator_bin ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = d, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator_bin",
  family_m = binomial()
)
paths(fit_m)
```

Now `a` is a log odds ratio and `b` is a change in the outcome per unit of the
mediator.

## Other families

Any `glm()` family works the same way, for example a count outcome:

```{r}
#| label: count-outcome
set.seed(1)
d$count <- rpois(nrow(d), exp(0.2 + 0.2 * d$mediator1))
fit_c <- fit_mediation(
  count ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1,
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1,
  data = d, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
  family_y = poisson()
)
class(fit_c)[1]
```

## Limits

- The four-way and joint decompositions need Gaussian identity-link models and
  stop with an informative error otherwise.
- Intervals for the product still come from the delta method or a bootstrap;
  see [Bootstrap Inference](bootstrap.html).
- Fitted `glm()` pairs can be extracted instead of fitted here:
  `extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y, ...)`.
